recent_posts.title: Bots and agents should identify themselves via Web Bot Auth
recent_posts.summary: Shopify is enforcing stricter rate limits on bots and agents accessing its Storefront API and hosted store pages. Unsigned requests now face the tightest restrictions. To qualify for higher rate limits, bot and agent operators must sign their requests using Web Bot Auth, an emerging IETF draft standard. Cloudflare's implementation guide is available as a reference. Merchants who want to crawl their own stores can find ready-to-use Web Bot Auth signatures in the Shopify admin.

recent_posts.title: Publish and unpublish product variants independently from product
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's API version 2026-07 introduces independent publishing control for product variants. Variants now implement the Publishable interface, allowing merchants and app developers to publish or unpublish individual variants per channel or catalog without deleting variants or duplicating products. The change is additive and non-breaking: product-level publishing still takes precedence, variants default to published, and existing apps require no modifications. New API fields support creating variants in an unpublished state, and product feed webhooks fire on variant publish/unpublish events.

recent_posts.title: More admin intents now support Settings
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has expanded its admin intents API with seven new Settings intents, building on the initial March release. Apps can now open contextual overlay editors for notifications, payment capture, gift cards, delivery profiles, and business details with a single API call. Each intent opens the relevant Settings page and scrolls merchants directly to the targeted field.

recent_posts.title: Inventory transfer webhooks include origin and destination location IDs, and mutation documentation clarified
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's Admin GraphQL API (2026-04 version) now includes origin and destination location IDs as Global IDs in inventory transfer webhook payloads, eliminating the need for extra API calls to determine transfer locations. The fields are omitted (not null) for older API versions or non-location transfers. Additionally, documentation for inventoryTransferSetItems and inventoryTransferRemoveItems mutations has been clarified to better describe upsert behavior, quantity handling on different transfer statuses, and no-op handling. Several error messages have also been made more descriptive, though error codes remain unchanged.

recent_posts.title: Default value of appliesOnSubscription changed to true for app discount inputs
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has changed the default value of the `appliesOnSubscription` field from `false` to `true` on the `DiscountCodeAppInput` and `DiscountAutomaticAppInput` GraphQL Admin API input types. No action is required from developers — the change has no effect on checkout discount behavior, and apps that explicitly set this field are unaffected. The update applies across all active API versions.

recent_posts.title: Monitor admin web vitals in the Dev Dashboard
recent_posts.summary: Shopify has moved admin performance dashboards from the Partner Dashboard to the Dev Dashboard. Developers can now access daily and 28-day P75 rollups for three Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) in one place. FID has been retired and replaced by INP. No code changes are required, and existing bookmarks will automatically redirect to the new location. The data shown matches what the App Store uses for Built for Shopify compliance evaluation.

recent_posts.title: Analytics metric targets now available in the GraphQL Admin API
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's GraphQL Admin API now supports analytics metric targets via four new operations: query, create, update, and delete. Merchants can set numeric goals for metrics like gross sales, track progress with visual gauges, and apps can read/write the same targets shown in the Shopify admin. Key features include deduplication by metric/date/filter, automatic status computation, and dimension-based filtering via ShopifyQL. Use cases include goal-setting apps, BI tools, planning apps, and agency dashboards. API version 2026-04 also adds two new ColumnDataType enum values for dimensionless scores and ratio/multiplier values.

recent_posts.title: Minor rounding change for custom line item discounts in POS 11.5
recent_posts.summary: Shopify POS 11.5 changes how fixed-amount custom line item discounts are calculated internally. Instead of applying the discount across the entire line, it will now be applied on a per-unit basis. This may cause rounding differences of up to one cent for amounts that don't divide evenly by quantity (e.g., a $5.00 discount on 3 items becomes $5.01). No action is required for extensions using API version 2026-04 or earlier, but a future API version will require passing per-unit discount amounts directly.

recent_posts.title: Scannable discount codes
recent_posts.summary: Shopify POS version 11.5 introduces scannable QR codes for discount codes. Merchants can generate QR codes from Shopify Admin that work at POS checkout and in online store sessions. No app changes are required, but developers who want to include QR codes as shareable links must replicate Shopify's URL-encoding format: simple codes encode directly, while special characters are double URL-encoded in the https://{shop}.myshopify.com/discount/{CODE} pattern.

recent_posts.title: Customer tax settings now available in Admin API
recent_posts.summary: Shopify's Admin GraphQL API version 2026-07 now exposes the taxSettings field on the Customer object publicly. Apps with the appropriate read customer data access scopes can query a customer's tax ID (e.g., VAT number) collected and validated during checkout. This is a read-only change returning the tax ID as a string or null. The validation status sub-field remains restricted to apps with approved protected customer data access. This aligns with existing B2B customer tax settings available since API version 2025-01.

top_posts.title: New CSS variable for mobile safe area insets
top_posts.summary: Shopify has introduced a new CSS custom property, `--shopify-safe-area-inset-bottom`, for embedded apps running on Shopify Mobile. Automatically set by App Bridge, it provides the pixel height of host UI overlays like the floating bottom navigation bar. Most apps require no changes since bottom padding is applied automatically, but apps with custom fixed-bottom elements (sticky footers, FABs) should use `var(--shopify-safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)` in their CSS to avoid content being obscured. The change takes effect April 15th, 2026.

top_posts.title: Now available: JS Buy SDK v3.0 — Shopify developer changelog
top_posts.summary: Shopify has released the final version of the JavaScript Buy SDK, v3.0, effective from March 14, 2025. The update aims to replace the deprecated Checkout API with the Cart API, albeit with some limitations. Developers must upgrade to this new version or switch to the Storefront API Client by July 1, 2025, to ensure their services remain operational.

top_posts.title: Reduced metafield value sizes
top_posts.summary: Starting with Shopify API version 2026-04, new metafield values will be capped at 16KB to improve platform performance and stability. Existing metafields exceeding this limit become read-only until updated. Developers needing to store larger data are advised to use alternatives such as metaobject references, list support, splitting data across multiple metafields, or the Files API. Shopify has also raised metaobject entry limits and increased metafield definition limits per resource to help accommodate larger data sets.

top_posts.title: Shopify Functions template and Shopify CLI changes to support Rust 1.84 — Shopify developer changelog
top_posts.summary: Shopify has updated its Functions templates to be compatible with Rust 1.84 by removing the incompatible cargo-wasi utility. Starting with Shopify CLI 3.73, all function builds now include an optimization pass by default, previously managed by cargo-wasi. These changes are effective from January 08, 2025, and compatible with Rust 1.78 and above.

top_posts.title: New developer documentation now available for Shopify Collective
top_posts.summary: New developer documentation for Shopify Collective is now available. This resource helps developers integrate with Shopify Collective, focusing on using APIs and webhooks to connect with external dependencies like third-party ERP and PIM solutions.
